claim: A formatted type's own MessagePack attributes are ignored unless the caller duplicates its contract in a surrogate. In the no-surrogate path, the collector unconditionally builds members with CreateContractlessMembers. For example, a type with [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored gets a contractless string-key formatter that serializes Ignored, instead of the required [Key]/[IgnoreMember] behaviour.

claim: The timestamp32 eligibility mask was inverted. nanoseconds shifted left by 34 always leaves the low 32 bits clear, so every positive-subsecond timestamp whose Unix seconds value is zero now takes the timestamp32 branch and loses its subsecond component. For example, 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z round-trips as 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z; a seconds value of 2^32 is likewise truncated by the 32-bit encoding.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129ReceiptTests.TimestampAtEpochWithSubsecondsRoundTrips. It serializes and deserializes 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z using MessagePackSerializer and fails on head because the result is the epoch without the 500 milliseconds. Also assert that an integral timestamp at Unix second 0 uses timestamp32 while a subsecond timestamp at that second uses timestamp64.

claim: The timestamp compact-encoding guard now tests the low 32 bits instead of the high 32 bits. An instant at the Unix epoch with nonzero subsecond nanoseconds therefore passes the timestamp32 path, which discards its nanoseconds; ordinary timestamps with nonzero seconds also lose the previous compact encoding. This changes the wire format and can corrupt deserialized values for existing users without any opt-in.
